common_name: Siemen Doorenbos Dahlia (Dwarf Pink Anemone-Flowered Dahlia with Cream Center)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; this dwarf anemone-flowered type stays compact and suits pots and border edges.

directions: A dwarf anemone-flowered dahlia bred in the Netherlands and named for Dutch dahlia hybridizer Siemen Doorenbos, this old heirloom produces 4-inch pink blooms with a dense, crumpled cushion of cream-white disc florets at the center, giving each flower a two-tiered look distinct from single or decorative types. Its compact, patio-friendly habit needs little staking. Pinch young plants once to encourage branching, deadhead to keep flowers coming from midsummer to frost, and lift and store tubers over winter where not reliably hardy.

common_name: Alfred Grille Dahlia (Coral-Pink Semi-Cactus Dahlia Shading to Yellow)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; stake plants early as the large semi-cactus blooms are heavy.

directions: A long-cultivated semi-cactus dahlia introduced in the mid-1960s, Alfred Grille produces large blooms up to 8 inches across in bright coral-pink shading to yellow toward the center, with long, pointed petals tightly rolled under and slightly twisted for a sea-anemone look. Give plants full sun and rich, well-drained soil, stake stems as flowers are large and heavy, and deadhead regularly to extend bloom from midsummer to frost; excellent as a cut flower thanks to its strong stems and vase life.

common_name: Honka White Dahlia (Pure White Star-Shaped Orchid Dahlia)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; this airy orchid-type dahlia is lighter in habit than decorative or ball types and needs only minimal staking.

directions: A white-flowered member of the star-shaped Honka orchid dahlia group, Honka White carries narrow, widely spaced petals radiating from a central disc into a clean, pure white star about 3 inches across. The open, airy flower form and wiry stems make it a favorite for cutting and for attracting pollinators. Pinch young plants to encourage branching, deadhead through the season, and lift and store tubers over winter where not reliably hardy.

common_name: Star Child Dahlia (Small White Orchid-Flowered Dahlia with Golden Centers)

planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally 4-6 inches deep once soil has warmed after last frost; Star Child is an early, prolific bloomer well suited to cutting gardens.

directions: An orchid-flowered dahlia from Swan Island Dahlias introduced in the early 1980s, Star Child bears delicate 3-inch white blooms with a soft touch of yellow at the petal base and radiant golden centers, held on strong, straight stems. It is typically one of the earliest dahlias to flower each season and continues prolifically into fall, making it a favorite for arrangements. Stake plants for support, deadhead regularly, and lift and store tubers over winter where not reliably hardy.
